question: What was the term for land revenue in the Chola kingdom?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kadamai.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In the Chola kingdom, the land revenue was known as Kadamai (कदमई), the basic land tax collected from cultivators.

• Land revenue was the main source of income for the Chola state, usually assessed as a share of the produce.

• Vetti was a form of forced/unpaid labour (a type of tax paid through service), not land revenue.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The Cholas maintained detailed land surveys and classified land for revenue purposes.

• Village assemblies like Ur, Sabha (Brahmadeya) and Nagaram helped in local administration and revenue collection.

• The Chola period (9th–13th century CE) is famous for local self-government and temple-centred economy.

NOTE

• Vetti (Option 1): A tax collected in the form of forced or unpaid labour in the Chola administration.

• Ladder tax (Option 2): Not a genuine Chola revenue term; a distractor option.

• Cess tax (Option 3): A general additional levy/surcharge, not the specific Chola term for land revenue.

question: Which of the following dynasty ruled India for only fifteen years?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Sur.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Sur dynasty (सूर वंश) ruled for only about fifteen years (1540–1555 CE), founded by Sher Shah Suri after defeating Humayun.

• Sher Shah Suri introduced far-reaching administrative and revenue reforms in this short span.

• After Sher Shah's death, weak successors led to the fall of the dynasty and the return of Humayun (Mughals) in 1555.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Sher Shah introduced the silver coin Rupiya and built/renovated the Grand Trunk Road (Sadak-e-Azam).

• His revenue system (Zabti/Ryotwari-type reforms) later influenced Akbar's administration.

• His tomb at Sasaram (Bihar) is a fine example of Indo-Islamic architecture.

NOTE

• Khilji (Option 2): Delhi Sultanate dynasty (1290–1320), famous for Alauddin Khilji; ruled about 30 years.

• Tughlaq (Option 3): Delhi Sultanate dynasty (1320–1414), ruled for around 90+ years.

• Lodi (Option 4): Last Delhi Sultanate dynasty (1451–1526), ended by Babur at the First Battle of Panipat.

question: Which of the following article of the Indian Constitution is related with Admission or establishment of new States?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Article 2.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Article 2 (अनुच्छेद 2) empowers Parliament to admit into the Union, or establish, new States on such terms and conditions as it thinks fit.

• Article 2 deals with new States that were NOT part of India earlier (external addition).

• It falls under Part I (The Union and its Territory) of the Constitution.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Article 1: Declares India, that is Bharat, shall be a Union of States.

• Article 3: Deals with formation of new States and alteration of areas, boundaries or names of existing States.

• Article 4: States that laws made under Articles 2 and 3 are not deemed to be amendments under Article 368.

NOTE

• Article 4 (Option 2): Relates to laws made under Articles 2 and 3 and consequential/supplemental matters.

• Article 8 (Option 3): Deals with rights of citizenship of persons of Indian origin residing outside India.

• Article 7 (Option 4): Deals with rights of citizenship of certain migrants to Pakistan.

question:
Which of the following statement is correct regarding the fundamental rights given in the Indian constitution?
I. Article 30 is related with Abolition of titles.
II. Article 22 is related with Prohibition of employment of children in factories, etc.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Neither I Nor II.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Both statements are incorrect regarding fundamental rights (मूल अधिकार).

• Article 30 is about the right of minorities to establish and administer educational institutions — NOT abolition of titles (that is Article 18).

• Article 22 deals with protection against arrest and detention — NOT prohibition of child employment (that is Article 24).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Article 18: Abolition of titles (except military and academic distinctions).

• Article 24: Prohibition of employment of children below 14 years in factories, mines and hazardous work.

• Article 21A: Right to education for children aged 6–14 years.

NOTE

• Only I (Option 1): Wrong, since Statement I wrongly links Article 30 to abolition of titles.

• Only II (Option 2): Wrong, since Statement II wrongly links Article 22 to child labour.

• Both I and II (Option 3): Wrong, because neither statement is correct.

question: Which Indian model was crowned Miss World in November 2017?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Manushi Chhillar.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Manushi Chhillar (मानुषी छिल्लर) was crowned Miss World 2017 in November 2017 at Sanya, China.

• She became the 6th Indian to win the Miss World title.

• She hails from Haryana and later entered the Hindi film industry.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Previous Indian Miss World winners include Reita Faria (1966), Aishwarya Rai (1994), Diana Hayden (1997), Yukta Mookhey (1999) and Priyanka Chopra (2000).

• Miss World is one of the oldest international beauty pageants, founded in 1951.

• Manushi's win came after a gap of 17 years for India (since 2000).

NOTE

• Lara Dutta (Option 1): Won Miss Universe 2000, not Miss World.

• Shilpa Singh (Option 3): Indian model who represented India at Miss Universe 2012; did not win Miss World.

• Harnaaz Sandhu (Option 4): Won Miss Universe 2021, not Miss World.

question: The Union Finance Minister in Budget 2025-26 announced to set up ______ Atal Tinkering Labs in Government schools in next 5 years.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 50000.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In the Union Budget 2025-26, the government announced setting up 50,000 Atal Tinkering Labs (ATLs) (अटल टिंकरिंग लैब) in government schools over the next 5 years.

• ATLs aim to foster innovation, creativity and problem-solving skills among school students.

• They are part of the Atal Innovation Mission (AIM) under NITI Aayog.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The Union Budget 2025-26 was presented by Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman.

• ATLs provide students hands-on exposure to STEM, robotics, 3D printing, IoT and electronics.

• The initiative supports the vision of a self-reliant, innovation-driven India.

NOTE

• 21000 (Option 1): Not the announced figure; a distractor.

• 75000 (Option 3): Incorrect figure for the ATL target.

• 100000 (Option 4): Incorrect; overstates the announced number of labs.

question: How many crimes under Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 now include increased imprisonment terms?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 33.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), 2023 (भारतीय न्याय संहिता), imprisonment terms have been increased for 33 offences.

• The BNS replaced the colonial-era Indian Penal Code (IPC), 1860.

• It came into effect from 1 July 2024, along with the BNSS and BSA.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The BNS introduced new provisions such as community service as a punishment and offences for terrorism and organised crime.

• Fines were increased in 83 offences and a mandatory minimum punishment was introduced in 23 offences.

• The three new criminal laws are BNS 2023, Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) 2023, and Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam (BSA) 2023.

NOTE

• 43 (Option 2): Incorrect count of offences with increased imprisonment.

• 63 (Option 3): Incorrect figure; a distractor.

• 13 (Option 4): Incorrect number; understates the figure.

question: Sakhi Niwas Scheme seen in news in April 2025 is related to which of the following?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Mission Shakti.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Sakhi Niwas (Working Women Hostel) scheme is a component under Mission Shakti (मिशन शक्ति).

• It provides safe and affordable accommodation for working women, along with day-care facilities for their children where possible.

• Mission Shakti is an umbrella scheme of the Ministry of Women and Child Development for women's safety, security and empowerment.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Mission Shakti has two sub-schemes: Sambal (safety and security) and Samarthya (empowerment).

• Sakhi Niwas falls under the Samarthya sub-scheme.

• Other components under Samarthya include One Stop Centres, Women Helpline, Shakti Sadan and Palna (creche).

NOTE

• Mission Vatsalya (Option 2): Scheme for child protection and child welfare services.

• Mission Durga (Option 3): Not a central WCD umbrella scheme; a distractor option.

• Mission Laxmi (Option 4): Not the scheme linked to Sakhi Niwas; a distractor.

question: The game of basketball originated in which of the following countries?
solution_text:
The correct answer is United states of America.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Basketball originated in the United States of America (संयुक्त राज्य अमेरिका).

• It was invented by Dr. James Naismith in 1891 at Springfield, Massachusetts.

• The game was created as an indoor activity to keep athletes fit during winter.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• A basketball team has 5 players on the court at a time.

• The sport became an Olympic event at the 1936 Berlin Olympics.

• The NBA (National Basketball Association) is the premier professional basketball league of the USA.

NOTE

• United Kingdom (Option 2): Home of many sports like cricket, football and rugby, but not basketball.

• South Africa (Option 3): Not the country of origin of basketball.

• Australia (Option 4): Not associated with the invention of basketball.

question: What was the total medal count for Tamil Nadu at the National Games 2025?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 92.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• At the 38th National Games 2025 (राष्ट्रीय खेल 2025) held in Uttarakhand, Tamil Nadu won a total of 92 medals.

• The National Games 2025 were hosted by Uttarakhand (its first time hosting the event).

• Services Sports Control Board (Services) topped the overall medal tally.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The 38th National Games 2025 were held from 28 January to 14 February 2025.

• The mascot of the Games was Mauli, inspired by the state bird Monal.

• The National Games promote sports talent across Indian states and union territories.

NOTE

• 68 (Option 2): Incorrect total medal figure for Tamil Nadu.

• 85 (Option 3): Incorrect figure; a distractor.

• 81 (Option 4): Does not match Tamil Nadu's medal count at the Games.

question: Which of the following sports does NOT include a ball?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Badminton.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Badminton (बैडमिंटन) does NOT use a ball; it is played with a shuttlecock and rackets.

• Cricket, Hockey and Soccer (Football) all involve a ball.

• Badminton can be played as singles or doubles across a net.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The governing body of world badminton is the Badminton World Federation (BWF).

• Famous Indian badminton players include P. V. Sindhu, Saina Nehwal and Pullela Gopichand.

• The Thomas Cup (men) and Uber Cup (women) are major team badminton championships.

NOTE

• Cricket (Option 1): Played with a hard leather ball and a bat.

• Hockey (Option 2): Played with a small hard ball and hockey sticks.

• Soccer (Option 3): Football, played with a spherical ball.

question: The endangered black collared yellow catfish found in Chalakudy river. This river is in ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kerala.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Chalakudy River flows through the state of Kerala (केरल).

• The endangered black collared yellow catfish is found in this river, known for its rich fish biodiversity.

• The Chalakudy River has one of the highest fish species diversity among Indian rivers.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The Chalakudy River is a tributary that joins the Periyar River system.

• The famous Athirappilly Waterfalls (largest waterfall in Kerala) is located on this river.

• Kerala's other major rivers include the Periyar, Bharathapuzha and Pamba.

NOTE

• Gujarat (Option 2): Its major rivers include Narmada, Tapi and Sabarmati, not Chalakudy.

• Maharashtra (Option 3): Major rivers include Godavari and Krishna, not Chalakudy.

• Haryana (Option 4): Rivers include Yamuna and Ghaggar; Chalakudy is not located here.

question: In March 2025, Prime Minister of India announced that cheetah introduction will be expanded to Gandhisagar Sanctuary, which is in ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Madhya Pradesh.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Gandhi Sagar Wildlife Sanctuary is located in Madhya Pradesh (मध्य प्रदेश).

• In March 2025, the cheetah reintroduction programme was announced to be expanded to Gandhi Sagar Sanctuary as a second home for cheetahs.

• It is situated in the Mandsaur and Neemuch districts along the Chambal River.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• India's Project Cheetah began in September 2022 with cheetahs brought to Kuno National Park (Madhya Pradesh) from Namibia and South Africa.

• Madhya Pradesh is often called the Tiger State and Cheetah State of India.

• The African cheetah is the world's fastest land animal.

NOTE

• Gujarat (Option 2): Home to the Gir National Park (Asiatic lions), not Gandhi Sagar Sanctuary.

• Maharashtra (Option 3): Has Tadoba and Melghat reserves; Gandhi Sagar is not here.

• Kerala (Option 4): Known for Periyar Reserve; not the location of Gandhi Sagar Sanctuary.

question: The 'Dedh Satara' musical instrument belongs to which Indian state?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Rajasthan.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The 'Dedh Satara' is a folk musical instrument belonging to the state of Rajasthan (राजस्थान).

• It is a wind instrument associated with the folk music traditions of the region.

• Rajasthan has a rich heritage of folk instruments and musician communities like the Manganiyars and Langas.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Other famous Rajasthani folk instruments include the Ravanhatha, Morchang, Algoza and Kamaycha.

• Rajasthani folk music is a major cultural attraction of the Thar desert region.

• Folk dances of Rajasthan include Ghoomar, Kalbelia and Bhavai.

NOTE

• Kerala (Option 1): Known for instruments like the Chenda and Idakka used in temple arts.

• Manipur (Option 2): Known for the Pung (drum) used in Manipuri dance.

• West Bengal (Option 3 text is Rajasthan; Option 4): Associated with instruments like the Baul ektara, not Dedh Satara.

question: At 800 km, a satellite in Sun Synchronous Orbit will travel at a speed of approximately ______ km per second.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 7.5.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A satellite in a Sun Synchronous Orbit (SSO) (सूर्य तुल्यकाली कक्षा) at about 800 km altitude travels at roughly 7.5 km per second.

• This is close to the typical orbital velocity of low Earth orbit satellites (~7.5–7.8 km/s).

• Orbital speed depends on altitude; lower orbits require higher speeds.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Sun Synchronous Orbits are near-polar orbits used for remote sensing and Earth observation satellites.

• In SSO, the satellite passes over a location at the same local solar time, ensuring consistent lighting.

• At about 7.5 km/s, a low Earth orbit satellite completes one revolution in roughly 90–100 minutes.

NOTE

• 1.5 (Option 1): Far too low for orbital velocity at this altitude.

• 15 (Option 2): Nearly double the actual orbital speed; incorrect.

• 22.5 (Option 3): Much higher than orbital velocity, close to escape-type speeds; incorrect.

question: A force of 10 N acts on an object. The object is displaced by 2 metres in the direction of the force. The force acts on the object all through the displacement. What is the work done?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 20 J.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Work done (कार्य) = Force × Displacement (when force and displacement are in the same direction).

• Here, Work = 10 N × 2 m = 20 Joules.

• Since the force acts along the displacement, the full force contributes to the work.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The SI unit of work is the Joule (J), where 1 J = 1 N·m.

• Work is a scalar quantity.

• General formula: W = F × d × cos θ, where θ is the angle between force and displacement; here θ = 0°, so cos θ = 1.

NOTE

• 5 J (Option 1): Incorrect; results from wrong calculation (e.g., 10 ÷ 2).

• 10 J (Option 2): Incorrect; equals only the force value, ignoring displacement.

• 15 J (Option 3): Incorrect; does not match F × d = 20 J.

question: HAL-developed 'Prachand' is which type of aircraft?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Light combat helicopter.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• 'Prachand' (प्रचंड) is a Light Combat Helicopter (LCH) developed by Hindustan Aeronautics Limited (HAL).

• It is designed for high-altitude warfare and can operate in terrains like Siachen and Ladakh.

• It is the first indigenous multi-role combat helicopter of India.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• LCH Prachand was formally inducted into the Indian Air Force in October 2022 at Jodhpur.

• It is equipped with air-to-air missiles, rockets and a 20 mm turret gun.

• HAL is a public sector defence undertaking headquartered in Bengaluru.

NOTE

• Fighter jet (Option 1): Prachand is a helicopter, not a fixed-wing fighter jet like the Tejas.

• Drone (Option 2): It is a manned helicopter, not an unmanned aerial vehicle.

• Civil passenger aeroplane (Option 3): It is a military combat helicopter, not a passenger aircraft.

question: Why is the low level of foreign exchange reserves a critical problem for India?
option_1: It means India is a lucrative place for investment.
option_2: It means India couldn't print money in future.
option_3: It means foreign citizens couldn't travel abroad.
option_4: It means India could barely afford to pay for essential imports for a very short time.
solution_text:
The correct answer is It means India could barely afford to pay for essential imports for a very short time.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Foreign exchange reserves (विदेशी मुद्रा भंडार) are used to pay for imports and to meet international obligations.

• A low level of forex reserves means the country can only afford essential imports (like crude oil) for a very short period.

• This threatens import cover, currency stability and the ability to repay external debt.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• India's forex reserves are managed by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI).

• Reserves include foreign currency assets, gold, SDRs and Reserve Tranche Position with the IMF.

• 'Import cover' measures the number of months of imports that reserves can finance.

NOTE

• Lucrative place for investment (Option 1): Low reserves generally discourage, not attract, investment.

• Couldn't print money in future (Option 2): Currency printing is governed by domestic monetary policy, not forex reserves.

• Foreign citizens couldn't travel abroad (Option 3): Forex reserve levels do not restrict foreign citizens' travel.

question: Which of the following statement is correct regarding money received by the government from loans and the sale of its own assets?
option_1: Loans create liability but sale of asset do not
option_2: Sale of asset create liability but loans do not
option_3: Loans are part of revenue receipts and sale of assets are part of capital receipts
option_4: Loans and sale of assets both do not reduces or increases the total amount of government financial assets
solution_text:
The correct answer is Loans create liability but sale of asset do not.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Both loans and sale of assets are capital receipts (पूँजीगत प्राप्तियाँ), but they differ in nature.

• Loans create a liability because they must be repaid in future.

• Sale of assets does NOT create a liability; it reduces the government's assets instead.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Capital receipts are those which either create a liability or reduce an asset.

• Revenue receipts neither create a liability nor reduce an asset (e.g., taxes).

• Borrowings, disinvestment and recovery of loans are examples of capital receipts.

NOTE

• Sale of asset create liability but loans do not (Option 2): Reversed and incorrect; loans create the liability.

• Loans are revenue receipts and sale of assets are capital receipts (Option 3): Wrong; both are capital receipts.

• Both do not reduce or increase financial assets (Option 4): Incorrect; sale of assets reduces assets and loans increase liabilities.

question: Which of the following was the capital of the kingdom of Tipu Sultan?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Seringapatam.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Seringapatam (Srirangapatna) (श्रीरंगपट्टम) was the capital of Tipu Sultan's kingdom of Mysore.

• It is located in present-day Karnataka, on an island in the Kaveri River.

• Tipu Sultan was killed here in 1799 during the Fourth Anglo-Mysore War against the British.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Tipu Sultan, the 'Tiger of Mysore', was the son of Hyder Ali.

• He is credited with the early military use of rockets (Mysorean rockets) against the British.

• The Fourth Anglo-Mysore War (1799) ended with Tipu's death and British dominance in South India.

NOTE

• Erode (Option 1): A city in Tamil Nadu; not Tipu Sultan's capital.

• Sira (Option 3): A town in Karnataka; not the capital of Tipu's kingdom.

• Chitradurga (Option 4): Known for its historic fort in Karnataka, but not Tipu's capital.

question: The national highways in India constitute only about ______ of the total road length but carry almost 40% of the road traffic.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 2%.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• National Highways (राष्ट्रीय राजमार्ग) constitute only about 2% of the total road length in India.

• Despite this small share, they carry nearly 40% of the total road traffic.

• This reflects the high importance of NHs in India's transport and freight movement.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• National Highways are maintained largely by the National Highways Authority of India (NHAI).

• Road transport is the dominant mode of transport in India.

• India has one of the largest road networks in the world.

NOTE

• 8% (Option 2): Overstates the share of national highways in total road length.

• 12% (Option 3): Incorrect; too high a proportion for NHs.

• 18% (Option 4): Incorrect; far exceeds the actual ~2% share.

question: On whose ideas was the second five year plan based?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Prasanta Chandra Mahalanobis.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Second Five Year Plan (1956–1961) was based on the ideas of Prasanta Chandra Mahalanobis (प्रशांतचंद्र महालनोबिस).

• It emphasised rapid industrialisation with focus on heavy and basic industries.

• The plan is also known as the Mahalanobis Model.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• P. C. Mahalanobis is regarded as the father of Indian statistics and founded the Indian Statistical Institute (ISI).

• National Statistics Day (29 June) is observed in his honour.

• The Second Plan led to setting up steel plants at Bhilai, Rourkela and Durgapur.

NOTE

• Chaudhari Charan Singh (Option 1): Former Prime Minister known for championing farmers' interests, not the plan model.

• Sardar Vallabh Bhai Patel (Option 2): India's first Home Minister and 'Iron Man', not linked to the plan model.

• K Kamraj (Option 3): Congress leader and former CM of Madras; not the basis of the Second Plan.

question:
Which of the following was the focus of the Industrial Policy Statement, 1991?
I. Allowing foreign investment by lowering controls and regulations
II. Exit policy for the sick units in private sector for a smooth exit without affecting welfare of labour
solution_text:
The correct answer is Both I and II.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Industrial Policy Statement, 1991 (औद्योगिक नीति वक्तव्य, 1991) marked the beginning of liberalisation, privatisation and globalisation (LPG) reforms.

• Statement I is correct: it allowed foreign investment by lowering controls and regulations.

• Statement II is correct: it provided an exit policy for sick units while protecting the welfare of labour.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The 1991 policy abolished industrial licensing for most industries (except a few).

• It reduced the number of industries reserved for the public sector.

• The reforms were introduced under PM P. V. Narasimha Rao and FM Dr. Manmohan Singh.

NOTE

• Only I (Option 1): Incorrect, since Statement II is also correct.

• Only II (Option 2): Incorrect, since Statement I is also correct.

• Neither I nor II (Option 4): Incorrect, as both statements accurately describe the 1991 policy.

question:
Which of the following is NOT a type of rural settlements?
I. Hamleted
II. Dispersed
solution_text:
The correct answer is Neither I nor II.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Both Hamleted and Dispersed ARE recognised types of rural settlements (ग्रामीण बस्तियाँ).

• Since both are valid types, neither statement fits the 'NOT a type' condition — hence the answer is Neither I nor II.

• Rural settlements are commonly classified based on their pattern and form.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Main types of rural settlements are Clustered/Compact, Semi-clustered/Hamleted, Dispersed and Scattered.

• A hamleted settlement is fragmented into several small units separated by physical or social factors.

• A dispersed settlement has isolated houses spread over a wide area, often in hilly or forested regions.

NOTE

• Only I (Option 1): Wrong, since Hamleted is indeed a type of rural settlement.

• Only II (Option 2): Wrong, since Dispersed is indeed a type of rural settlement.

• Both I and II (Option 3): Wrong, because both are valid rural settlement types.

question: What are the end products of pyruvate during fermentation process?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Ethanol and carbon dioxide.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• During alcoholic fermentation (किण्वन), pyruvate is broken down into ethanol and carbon dioxide.

• This is an anaerobic process (occurs in the absence of oxygen), commonly carried out by yeast.

• Fermentation allows organisms to regenerate NAD+ so that glycolysis can continue.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• In muscle cells, anaerobic respiration converts pyruvate into lactic acid instead of ethanol.

• Fermentation is used to produce bread, alcohol, curd, cheese and other products.

• Glycolysis first converts glucose into pyruvate before fermentation begins.

NOTE

• Methanol and nitrogen (Option 2): Not the products of pyruvate fermentation.

• Methanol and hydrogen (Option 3): Incorrect; fermentation yields ethanol, not methanol.

• Glucose and helium (Option 4): Incorrect; glucose is the starting material and helium is not involved.
